summary: Scheduled dashboard snapshots drop templated filters when retention compaction runs
description:
Issue summary: Scheduled dashboard snapshot job for Acme Payments ran on 2026-02-20 03:00 UTC and produced a snapshot where all dashboard template variables (org_id, env_filter, payment_region) were reset to org defaults instead of the user's saved filter values. Impact: alerts tied to thresholds on that snapshot evaluated against the wrong filter set and triggered escalations to on-call. Environment: Production, us-east; customer on enterprise plan with custom retention set to 'strict-30d' which triggers background compaction.

Observed behavior: Saved dashboard variables are preserved when a snapshot is generated interactively from the Console UI, but the scheduled export runner path loses per-snapshot templated filter state when a retention compaction event overlaps the export window. Expected behavior: Scheduled snapshots should honor saved variable values and run with the same filter set as interactive snapshots.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create a dashboard with templated variables: org_id (non-default), env_filter (staging), payment_region (eu-west).
2) Save the dashboard and create a scheduled snapshot to run daily at 03:00 UTC.
3) Configure org retention to strict-30d and force a background compaction to start during the same maintenance window.
4) Observe generated snapshot file and the alert evaluation attached to it.
5) Compare variable values between interactive snapshot (Save -> Snapshot now) and the scheduled snapshot file.

Notes: Reproducible in prod with compaction on. Intermittent in staging unless compaction window intentionally overlapped.

comments: Support (Aisha Patel) 2026-02-20: Customer reported that scheduled snapshots are returning dashboard variables set to org defaults. They attached the scheduled snapshot JSON and the interactive snapshot for comparison. First response sent; escalated to eng because they hit on-call alerts.

SRE (Daniel Kim) 2026-02-21: Reproduced in prod by overlapping compaction. Observed export-worker falling back to var cache when compaction holds a partition lock. Hypothesis: scheduled export path queries the live variable index which is temporarily unavailable during compaction, causing fallback to global defaults.

Eng (Priya Ramesh) 2026-02-22: Reviewed export-worker code path (console/exporter/scheduler). Noticed an edge-case where variable resolution uses the 'live_index' API which returns 503 during compaction. Suggested fallback behavior needs to prefer persisted saved-vars snapshot rather than global defaults. Opening PR to change exporter to use persisted snapshot store when present. See PR #1482.
Support (Aisha Patel) 2026-02-23: Customer confirmed they saw two false-positive alerts and provided the escalation screenshots. Asked for ETA for fix and whether a backfill is possible.

Eng (Daniel Kim) 2026-02-24: Hotfix deployed to prod: exporter now retries persisted-snapshot store and falls back to last-known-saved-vars before global defaults. Backfill plan: re-run exports for 2026-02-20..2026-02-22 for Acme Payments and re-evaluate alerts. Notifying customer of scheduled backfill run on 2026-02-25.
investigation_notes:
- Repro steps validated in staging with controlled compaction window.
- Root cause: exporter used volatile 'live_index' for resolving templated vars which is unavailable during retention compaction. Global defaults were used as a last-resort fallback incorrectly.
- Related behavior: interactive snapshots call 'persisted_snapshot_service' which contains the saved variable set; scheduled exporter did not.
- Related PR: console#1482 modifies exporter to prefer persisted_snapshot_service with retry/backoff; includes unit tests and an integration test that simulates a compaction-induced live_index 503.
- Observability: added metric exporter.snapshot.var_resolution_source (values: persisted, live, default) to track frequency.
- Cross-references: slack #support (thread TS123456), confluence runbook page for scheduled exports.
resolution:
Hotfix applied 2026-02-24: exporter now attempts persisted_snapshot_service first, retries live_index with exponential backoff, and only then falls back to global defaults. Backfill scheduled for 2026-02-25 to regenerate snapshots for affected days and re-evaluate alerts for Acme Payments. Follow-up: full rollout and additional tests in PR #1482.

Rollout notes: Hotfix rolled to us-east only initially (canary) then to global. Monitoring: exporter.snapshot.var_resolution_source metric recorded; no further fallbacks to default observed in canary window.

Customer communication: Support informed customer on 2026-02-24 and scheduled backfill on 2026-02-25; offered credit for noise and support assistance during backfill.
follow_up_actions:
- Engineering to merge PR #1482 and run integration tests in staging (owner: Priya Ramesh)
- Add unit/integration tests for compaction overlap to prevent regression
- Run analytics to find other scheduled export jobs that used fallback defaults in the last 30 days and schedule backfills where needed (owner: DataInfra)
- Update scheduled export runbook to include compaction overlap guidance and recommended maintenance windows (owner: SRE)
- Notify Trust & Safety if any alerts were paged to on-call outside SLA (owner: Support)
